title: Regret-Minimization Battlecards — Enterprise Inference
summary: Compact battlecards for AE/SEs focused on ‘regret-minimization’ when pitching Redwood for enterprise inference. Combines SLO-first framing, fallback economics, and pilot acceptance criteria so buyers feel safe choosing Redwood without over-committing to unknown operational risk.
body:
Status: rough draft / for internal review

Goal: give field teams a tight, evidence-backed scripting guide that reduces buyer regret risk (technical, financial, and compliance) during evaluation and procurement. Use in discovery calls, technical workshops, and procurement reviews.

Top-level thesis (1 line): Buyers sign when they can reduce the downside of a wrong bet — we position Redwood as the low-regret option because of predictable performance, graceful fallbacks, and clear pilot-to-production runbooks.

Who to use this with (persona cues):
- Platform Architects / Integration Architects: care about predictable throughput, network topology, and migration risk. Signal: asking about burst behavior, private deployment requirements, SLAs.
- ML/Inference Engineers: care about latency distributions, cold-starts, kv-cache behavior. Signal: questions on batching, quantization, or exact model kernels.
- Procurement / Security / Compliance: care about contracts, audit, data flow. Signal: requests for SOC2, KMS, and VPC diagrams.

Buyer pain framing (scripts / triggers):
- "We can’t afford a month of downtime while we migrate models." -> highlight fallbacks and canary rollouts.
- "We’ll get big cost spikes once usage grows." -> show committed vs burst pricing, Optimize suggestions.
- "We need predictable latencies for user-facing product SLAs." -> surface latency percentiles and Dedicated commitments.

One-sentence value lines by persona:
- Platform Architect: "Same API, predictable SLOs, and a migration path that lets you pilot without changing your infra."
- ML Engineer: "We preserve model fidelity while cutting per-token cost via batching, KV caching, and quantization suggestions—no re-training required."
- Procurement: "Contracted capacity + audit-ready logs = lower operational risk and clearer TCO."

Regret-minimization play (how we reduce regret):
1) Small, fast pilot (2–4 weeks) with measurable success criteria (latency p95 < X, cost per 1k tokens < Y, inference error delta < Z).
2) Canary deploy plan: stepwise rollout to production with auto-fallback to hosted variants if Dedicated capacity is constrained.
3) Financial guardrails: commit band + burst bucket + transparent overage logic.
4) Compliance package for pilot: limited data retention, audit logging, optional private control plane.

Pilot acceptance criteria (example template AEs can copy):
- Latency: p95 under 120ms for synthetic production mix (see appendix test script link).
- Availability: 99.9% during business hours for pilot window.
- Quality: Top-3 F1 on NLU test set within 3% of baseline model.
- Cost: projected monthly unit cost within 10% of agreed target for expected QPS.
- Security: SCM and logs integrated with customer KMS during pilot.

Objection handling (short scripts):
- "What if latency spikes under load?" -> "We can route traffic via a lower-latency region or fallback to a compatible model with identical prompts; we’ll predefine rollout thresholds and alerting for immediate rollback."
- "How do we avoid runaway costs?" -> "Reserved capacity + burst controls + token-level cost dashboards; we’ll run a 2-week load projection during pilot and lock billing alerts at thresholds you set."
- "Are we locked to Redwood?" -> "No — same API surface and exportable versions; you control model pins and we keep model artifacts/version manifests for migration planning."

Competitive map (headline bullets — use at-a-glance in calls):
- Large cloud providers (managed endpoints): commoditized infra, weaker inference optimizations, higher unit cost at production scale. Advantage: bundling with infra.
- LLM API-focused providers: simple experience but limited control over SLOs and private deployments. Advantage: quick start.
- Self-hosted inference stacks: max control but high ops cost and longer time-to-first-response. Advantage: cost at massive scale if team builds ops.

Tactical playbook (AE/SE steps during a 45-minute evaluation call):
1) 0–8 min: Quick trust-build (benchmarks, customer example with similar constraints).
2) 8–18 min: Discovery — probe for SLOs, data, compliance must-haves. Use persona cues above.
3) 18–28 min: Sketch pilot (sample QPS, latency target, success metrics). Leave placeholders to email later.
4) 28–38 min: Objection handling + financial anchors (present commit + burst).
5) 38–45 min: Next steps: technical workshop, NDA, or procurement packet. Book follow-up.

Pricing anchors (talk track, not legal):
- Entry pilot: small reserved pool for 2–4 weeks with capped burst; unit cost higher than committed production but includes SRE/SE support.
- Production reserved: discounted unit cost, SLA-backed.
- Optimize add-on: tech suggestions that can reduce per-token cost ~15–40% depending on workload.

Red team / risk scenarios to highlight (be transparent):
- Sudden model quality regression after an upstream model change -> mitigation: pinned model versions + automated eval suites + canary holdback.
- Regional outage -> mitigation: cross-region routing + failover policy; degrade to hosted fallback.
- Unpredicted cost spikes from adversarial traffic -> mitigation: rate limit + alerting + configurable per-token caps.

Appendix (quick links and test artifacts to share after call):
- Mini test harness: link to synthetic load script (connected ticket) — copyable and runnable by customer infra.
- Canary checklist: checklist of steps for a safe 10% -> 50% rollout.
- Eval template: minimal prompt sets and automated metrics we run during pilot.

Open questions / TODO for product & SRE before we formalize:
- Add canned synthetic profiles for common verticals (support agent, search reranking, summarization) — need infra team to produce sample p95/p50 baselines.
- Create one-click pilot bundle in Console that preconfigures reserved pool + alerts + privacy toggles. (PRF: product ticket needed)
- Pricing language: legal needs clear sample pilot contract term.

Internal notes / quick reminders:
- This doc is meant to be a single-sheet companion to longer playbooks — keep it short for AEs.
- Use numbers where possible; avoid vague words like "fast" without a metric.
- When in doubt, default to risk reduction framing rather than capability bragging.

Sample email follow-up template (AE copy-paste):
Subject: Next steps — Redwood pilot plan and success criteria
Body: Hi <Name>, great conversation today. Per our call, attached is the 2–4 week pilot outline: target p95 <120ms, availability 99.9% (business hours), and quality delta target <3% vs baseline. We’ll provide the synthetic test harness and a step-by-step canary checklist. Can we schedule a 60-min technical workshop next week to lock the pilot config?

---
Freeform brainstorm bits (notes to self):
- Consider an ROI calculator that shows time-to-no-regret (months until self-hosting ops exceed cost of Redwood + team ramp)
- Quick-case: "What if we lose Redwood?" one-pager: migration steps and export artifacts.
- Customer proof snippet: anonymized numbers from early Dedicated customer (need permission).

End of draft.
